errors.english: that which is not produced by a person [note: referring to the superhuman origins claimed for Vedic scripture]
errors.why: dbang du ma byas pa means 'what is not under (a speaker's) control', i.e. not governed by intention; it is not the word for 'not made by a person' (skyes bus ma byas pa), which the text uses separately a few lines later.

note: A sound rendering of the argument against an authorless word; the verse/commentary boundaries are a little blurred but the reasoning is carried correctly.

errors.english: Because it transcends that, it is "anta" meaning indestructible.
errors.why: The gloss etymologises shin tu = atyanta (ati + anta): anta is destruction, what goes beyond it is atyanta, the indestructible; rendering shin tu as 'extreme' and the result as 'anta' loses the etymology.

errors.english: To explain the meaning of the gathering:
errors.why: 'dus par bya ba'i phyir means 'for the sake of brevity': the second half-stanza doubles as the fourth, so it is abbreviated; it is not an explanation of 'the gathering'.

note: Generally follows the commentary on the seed syllables and the Apabhraṃśa song, but the etymological glosses (atyanta) and the remark on the stanza structure are garbled.

errors.why: The lemma is phyir from the root text's de'i phyir, 'for the sake of that' (i.e. preparatory acts done for the robe), not 'furthermore'.

fix.replace: The term "for the sake of [it]" indicates

errors.english: the phrases "repeatedly desiring," "to whatever small extent," and "all" are established as the rule
errors.why: yang dang yang du 'dod pa can qualifies the words 'however little' and 'all' as having distributive (repetitive) sense; it is not a third quoted phrase meaning 'repeatedly desiring'.

errors.english: without having been appointed to accomplish one's own purpose
errors.why: The monk approaches the weaver merely out of pleasure without instructing him to do anything for his own purpose; he is the one who does not give orders, not one who was not appointed.

note: Usable account of the weaving rule and its preliminary offences, but several commentarial lemmas and grammatical remarks are misread.

errors.english: they should remain simply by looking at the food
errors.why: zan la bltas pa tsam gyis is idiomatic: they are to stay with only food as their due (receiving meals but no share of gains), not literally 'looking at the food'.

note: A faithful rendering of the rules on duties, shares and meals at other monasteries, with one over-literal idiom.

errors.english: There is also no connection between the definition of emptiness and that which arises from it, because it is eternal.
errors.why: After ruling out identity-relation, the text rules out the second relation, the one 'characterised as arising from it' (tadutpatti), with emptiness; 'definition of emptiness' misparses mtshan nyid.

fix.find: There is also no connection between the definition of emptiness and that which arises from it, because it is eternal.
fix.replace: Nor is there, with emptiness, a relation whose character is arising from it (tadutpatti), because emptiness is permanent.

errors.english: Because things [note: as independent entities] do not exist, emptiness is not an effect
errors.why: The reason is that emptiness itself is a non-entity (abhāva), and so cannot be an effect; it does not say that things do not exist.

fix.find: Because things [note: as independent entities] do not exist, emptiness is not an effect
fix.replace: Because emptiness is a non-entity (abhāva), it is not an effect

errors.english: The very nature of birth, occurring in the beginningless cycle of existence for those with an obsession with things, is a cause of delusion regarding the vision of the true meaning.
errors.why: The subject that is 'poison' is the clinging to things (dngos po la mngon par zhen pa), whose nature is to arise throughout beginningless saṃsāra; 'birth' is not the subject.

fix.find: The very nature of birth, occurring in the beginningless cycle of existence for those with an obsession with things, is a cause of delusion regarding the vision of the true meaning.
fix.replace: The clinging to things, whose nature is to arise throughout beginningless existence in saṃsāra, is itself a cause of intoxication regarding the vision of the true meaning.

note: The word-by-word commentary is followed, but key steps of the argument (the two relations, emptiness as non-entity, what the poison is) are misconstrued.

errors.english: When they attain the second meditative concentration, and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, because they have not experienced those specific objects, they develop the perception of being an Arhat while in that first meditative concentration.
errors.why: The meditator who has attained only the first dhyāna, not having experienced the domain of those who attain the second up to the summit, conceives the first dhyāna to be arhatship; the English has him attaining the higher states.

fix.find: When they attain the second meditative concentration, and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, because they have not experienced those specific objects, they develop the perception of being an Arhat while in that first meditative concentration.
fix.replace: Not having experienced the domain of those who attain the second meditative concentration and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, they conceive of that first meditative concentration as arhatship.

errors.english: the texts of the Vaisheshika [note: a non-Buddhist school of Indian philosophy]
errors.why: In this Vinaya commentary the source for the two origins of the view (reasoning and absorption) is the Abhidharma Vibhāṣā tradition, not the non-Buddhist Vaiśeṣika; the note compounds the error.

note: The four-truths analysis of the arhat formula is fine; the account of how meditators come to deny arhats is inverted.

errors.english: the clarity or lack of clarity of the mind
errors.why: dang ba here is faith/serene confidence (prasāda), as the resumed root line dang ba'i yid kyis dngos grub thob shows; 'clarity of mind' misses the sense.

note: A good rendering of the foam-bubble simile, the two truths, and the humoral timing of dreams, with one doubtful term.

The ritual for expelling obstructers and the arrangement of the vessels is rendered faithfully; some obscure dance-step lines are paraphrased loosely but not misrepresented in a way a specialist would flag with confidence.

errors.english: It was for this purpose that I was earnestly sought after by that brahmin [note: referring to the messengers or the father].
errors.why: Pippalāyana says that it was for his sake that she ('you') was earnestly asked for in marriage by that brahmin (yatkṛte tena vipreṇa tvaṃ prayatnena yācitā).

fix.find: It was for this purpose that I was earnestly sought after by that brahmin [note: referring to the messengers or the father].
fix.replace: It is for my sake that you were earnestly asked for in marriage by that brahmin.

errors.english: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], who possessed boundless and increasing wealth, having examined the matter, gave
errors.why: Kapila examined HIM, the groom of boundless wealth (tam anantadhanodayam samanviṣya); the wealth is the groom's, not Kapila's.

fix.find: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], who possessed boundless and increasing wealth, having examined the matter, gave
fix.replace: Kapila [note: the father of the bride], having examined him, a man of boundless and increasing wealth, gave

note: A fluent rendering of the Pippalāyana-Bhadrā verses, but two case-role errors misattribute who was sought and whose wealth was examined.

errors.english: Therefore, because they are mutually exclusive, the positions of being either identical or distinct are both illogical.
errors.why: Having refuted 'distinct' and 'non-distinct' separately, the text now refutes the third alternative, that manifestation is BOTH distinct and non-distinct, before the fourth ('neither').

fix.find: Therefore, because they are mutually exclusive, the positions of being either identical or distinct are both illogical.
fix.replace: Therefore, because they are mutually contradictory, the position that they are both distinct and non-distinct is also illogical.

note: A clear rendering of the refutation of Sāṃkhya manifestation/transformation, except that the tetralemma's third position is misread.
